candidate.profile: Finite rules (lhs,rhs) over exact D1 bit-words {0,1}, lhs nonempty, |rhs|<|lhs|. Rewriting replaces any contiguous occurrence (including overlaps) of lhs by rhs, no ordered-rule priority and no strategy. Full rewriting is nondeterministic. rhs may be empty. Rules treated as a set, duplicate rules harmless. Empty starting word has no rewrites.
candidate.law: Compute all same-source one-step peaks arising from overlapping (including nested) occurrences of any pair of left sides. Each critical pair is joinable iff its two descendants share at least one reachable normal form under the same rules. Because every rule strictly shortens finite words, termination is proved by exact length. Then all critical pairs joinable is equivalent to confluence of the entire finite string rewrite relation (critical pair criterion + Newman's lemma). Return CONFLUENT or a concrete NONCONFLUENT witness: source, two branches, and separately reachable normal-form sets with empty intersection. Wording does not imply that a nonconfluent ruleset lacks individual common normal forms for other starting words.
candidate.signature: (ordered finite list of (nonempty-binary-lhs, strictly-shorter-binary-rhs))->CONFLUENT or NONCONFLUENT(witness)

witnesses.reason: 00→0 is length-decreasing; overlapping runs of zeros converge
critical peak 010 reduces to 00 by either branch
010 can yield 00 or 01 and subsequently 0; direct normal-form witness may vary, compute oracle, don't assert exact branches blindly
no redex, reflexive closure is confluent

falsifiers: Never count disjoint non-overlapping redex occurrences as unjoinable critical conflicts; the two orders commute.
Two peaks may differ immediately yet be joinable later; comparing only first descendants is unsound.
Identical left sides with distinct right sides yield a critical peak; omitting containment or same-position overlaps misses a real conflict.
Do not invoke termination/Newman's lemma for length-preserving, length-growing, cyclic or unrestricted higher-order rewrite systems.
Do not return a nonconfluence witness without two reachable branches whose normal-form sets are disjoint.
